title: Backstop Implementation Spec Schema v1
description: Schema for implementation specifications with claims-based verification traceability. Extends backstop-artifact-base-v1.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Live: draft, ready-for-implementation, implemented. Terminal/end-of-life: replaced (superseded by a named successor — requires replaced-by), canceled (work abandoned), deprecated (retired without a single named successor), obsoleted (delivered then removed with no 1:1 successor — requires obsoleted-by).

obsoleted-by.description: Required when status is `obsoleted`. A typed artifact id naming the work that removed this delivered-then-removed capability with no 1:1 successor. Documentary only; enforced in pkg/validate/terminal.go.

spec_version.description: Semantic version of the spec itself

implementation.description: Implementation target details. 'subject' names the language-neutral unit under test (the substantiveness noTarget guard checks that each mandated test references it). 'package' is accepted as a deprecated alias for 'subject' on legacy specs.

requirements.description: REQ-NNN functional requirements — what must be true. Optional 'supports' traces back to bundle requirement(s) (format: bundle-name:REQ-NNN). Optional 'follows' binds standard rule references (STD-LANG-NNN:RULE-ID) or lowercase-kebab recipe names.

claims.description: CLM-NNN claims — atomic verification units mapping to test functions, each tracing to a REQ. Optional 'subject' overrides the spec-level implementation.subject for this claim's mandated test(s), so a spec whose claims span multiple units can declare each claim's own target (claims without it inherit the spec default). Optional 'kind: absence' marks the claim's mandated test(s) as absence/structural (they prove something is ABSENT and by design do not reference the target subject), which skips the noTarget substantiveness join for those tests.

contracts.description: API surface contracts — each entry declares a file's provides (exported symbols) and consumes (dependencies)

capabilities.description: Optional UC-NNN references linking this spec to user capabilities. If present, must be non-empty with valid unique IDs.
